topic: active clustering; protein sequence analysis; metric assumptions
status: bounded within-lineage empirical tension; external validation required
claim: Two primary studies from the same research group show that limited-distance landmark clustering can use few one-versus-all queries and recover most tested Pfam sequence-family labels when the objective-stability/separation assumptions fit the data, but the original k-median method is less accurate on SCOP structural superfamily labels and on selected Pfam sets. A follow-up objective variant improved some original failure cases (Pfam sets 7 and 9), but not most Pfam sets, and did not establish independent generalization. This suggests that label–distance-modality alignment and assumption diagnostics may determine transfer more than query count alone.

sources.title: Efficient Clustering with Limited Distance Information
locators: §§1–3 and Theorem 2: approximation-stability and cluster-size conditions for O(k+log(1/delta)) one-versus-all queries
§§5.1–5.3: median-over-runs Pfam/SCOP experiments, parameter sensitivity, SCOP counterexample
§6: large target clusters and future work

sources.title: Min-Sum Clustering of Protein Sequences with Limited Distance Information
locators: §1: changed objective and relation to original k-median method
§5: same datasets, matched query budget, improvements on Pfam 7/9 but not most Pfam sets; SCOP comparisons

interpretation: The two works are from the same team and reuse benchmark datasets, so their contrast is useful evidence about assumption/metric sensitivity but is not independent replication. The candidate concerns whether a pre-analysis diagnostic can predict algorithm transfer or trigger abstention; no global novelty claim is made.
falsifiable_question: Can label-free diagnostics computed from a small distance-query budget predict when k-median landmark clustering will fail because the available distance modality does not align with the target task? Does a pre-registered selector among k-median, min-sum, and abstention improve held-out-family accuracy at fixed query cost on Pfam, SCOP, and independent protein datasets?
primary_outcome: Held-out family/superfamily clustering error, query count, coverage/abstention rate, and calibration of predicted failure; split by protein family and database version to prevent leakage.
counterevidence_and_caveats: Both papers are from the same team; the min-sum paper is not independent replication.
The second paper reuses the original Pfam/SCOP benchmark datasets and gold labels.
Formal guarantees require stability assumptions and minimum target-cluster sizes; assumptions may fail in datasets with outliers or small clusters.
SCOP labels use structural/biochemical evidence while the query distance is sequence-based, so poor performance may reflect target mismatch rather than clustering alone.
Only a few dataset families and manually chosen parameters were examined; results do not establish a universal modality-alignment effect.
suggested_design: Freeze versions of Pfam/SCOP plus at least two independent sequence collections; split by family and collection version. At each fixed query budget, compute unlabeled distance-distribution/clusterability diagnostics, choose k-median/min-sum/abstain using training families only, and compare with each fixed method on held-out families. Report error and coverage jointly, repeated seeds, and sensitivity to small clusters/outliers.
